short: Vandal fire ships destroyed the largest fleet Rome ever assembled, ending the last real chance to retake Africa.
full:
In 468 CE, the eastern and western Roman empires jointly launched one of the largest amphibious operations of antiquity, reportedly over a thousand ships and tens of thousands of troops, under the eastern commander Basiliscus, aiming to destroy the Vandal kingdom and recover Africa's grain lands. Rather than pressing his advantage after landing near Carthage, Basiliscus accepted the Vandal king Geiseric's request for a five-day truce to negotiate terms.

Geiseric used the delay to load ships with combustible material and, aided by a favourable wind, sent them into the anchored Roman fleet at Cape Bon. Roughly half the fleet was destroyed and Basiliscus fled with the survivors. The catastrophe emptied the eastern treasury and ended the last serious attempt to reverse Vandal control of North Africa, leaving the western empire without its grain supply and its Mediterranean seaways at the invaders' mercy in the years before its final collapse.
